Context: the previous page ends with symmetric (2,2)-forms in two variables s,z of the type (s-z)(sz-1)(α sz+β z+γ s+δ), together with product relations such as x1x2=x3x4 and x1ξ1x2ξ2=f^2, and pairing schemes like αγ, αδ, αγ', αδ'. This page continues with bilinear forms in (s,z).

(1) Riemann sets up four bilinear forms in (s,z):
x1=(s-α)(z-β)+a(s-z)
x2=(s-α)(z-γ)+b(s-z)
x3=(s-δ)(z-β)+c(s-z)
x4=(s-δ)(z-γ)+d(s-z)
Remark (mine): each x_i vanishes at two points of the diagonal s=z. x1 vanishes at (α,α) and (β,β); x2 at α,γ; x3 at δ,β; x4 at δ,γ. The 'leading parts' satisfy (s-α)(z-β)·(s-δ)(z-γ) = (s-α)(z-γ)·(s-δ)(z-β). Hence x1x4 - x2x3 ≡ 0 mod (s-z). This is the analogue of the relation x1x4 = x2x3 of the previous page, holding modulo the diagonal.

(2) Elimination giving a factorisation. b·x1 - a·x2 = (s-α)((b-a)z - (βb-γa)). The a(s-z) and b(s-z) terms cancel and the common factor (s-α) splits off. So this member of the pencil spanned by x1,x2 is reducible.

(3) Rewriting with the roles of s and z exchanged. Since (s-α)(z-β)-(s-β)(z-α) = (α-β)(s-z), one gets
x1 = (s-β)(z-α) + (a+α-β)(s-z)
x2 = (s-γ)(z-α) + (b+α-γ)(s-z).
Hence (b+α-γ)x1 - (a+α-β)x2 = (z-α)·[(b-a+β-γ)s - (βb-γa+αβ-αγ)]. Riemann writes only the beginning '(z-α)((b-a+β-γ)…', with the variable struck through and the bracket left unfinished. So the pencil ⟨x1,x2⟩ contains exactly two reducible members: one containing the line s=α, the other the line z=α (their common diagonal point).

(4) He considers the square (P + (s-z)f)^2, where P=(s-α)(z-β)(s-δ)(z-γ) and f is an undetermined form. Next to it he writes (-a(s-δ)(z-γ)+f)^2. The implicit step (mine) is the substitution (s-α)(z-β) = x1 - a(s-z). This gives P + (s-z)f = x1(s-δ)(z-γ) + (s-z)(f - a(s-δ)(z-γ)). So on the curve x1=0 the square reduces to (s-z)^2(f - a(s-δ)(z-γ))^2. Presumably this is aimed at representing a symmetric (2,2)-relation as a square modulo x1 (cf. x1ξ1x2ξ2=f^2 on the previous page).

(5) Bottom left: a table of the factors s-α, z-α / s-β, z-β, and dot-and-circle schemes. These record which linear factors (which diagonal points) each form contains. Below them are pairings of letters with primed versions (αγ, αγ', α'γ', ββ', …), continuing the incidence bookkeeping of the previous page.
